categories.name: Computer
categories.blurb: Desktop and a small Linux computer

items.name: MyoWare 2.0 Muscle Sensor
items.desc: A sensor that picks up the tiny electrical signal a muscle makes when it flexes. He'll use it to detect muscle activity in his wearable fitness tracker.

items.name: MyoWare Electrodes (pack of 6) ×3
items.desc: Sticky skin pads that let the muscle sensor read the signal. Each test uses three and they're single-use, so three packs cover about six sessions.

items.name: 500 mAh Rechargeable Battery
items.desc: A small rechargeable lithium-polymer battery with built-in protection. It powers the wearable without a cable and is small enough for a wrist or waist unit.

items.name: Adafruit ESP32-S3 Feather
items.desc: A tiny programmable board with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and a USB-C port that also charges the battery. It's the brain of the wearable.

items.name: STEMMA QT / Qwiic Cable Kit (10 cables)
items.desc: A set of 10 plug-in cables in assorted lengths that connect sensors and boards together with no soldering. The Qwiic and STEMMA QT connectors are the same.

items.name: VL53L1X Time-of-Flight Distance Sensor
items.desc: A distance sensor that measures how far away things are using an invisible laser pulse, for robotics projects.

items.name: AMG8833 Thermal Camera
items.desc: An 8x8-pixel heat camera that shows where the warmest spots are in front of it. For robotics projects that need to find or point at heat.

items.name: Mini Pan-Tilt Kit
items.desc: A small assembled bracket with two tiny motors that tilts and swivels whatever is mounted on it. It will aim sensors in robotics projects.

items.name: PCA9685 16-Channel Servo Driver
items.desc: A control board that runs up to 16 small motors (servos) smoothly from one board. It lets him drive the pan-tilt kit and later robot arms.

items.name: Audio-Technica AT-LP120XUSB Turntable
items.desc: A direct-drive record player with a USB output, so records can also be saved to a computer.

items.name: Dayton Audio MK KIT Bookshelf Speaker Kit (pair)
items.note: Backordered at Parts Express on Nov 26, the only seller found; it ships when restocked.
items.desc: A pair of speakers he builds himself from matched drivers, crossovers and flat-pack wooden cabinets. A build project that ends in real speakers.

items.name: Fosi Audio BT20A Pro Amplifier
items.desc: A compact stereo amplifier with Bluetooth that powers the speakers and takes wired and wireless inputs.

items.name: 14 AWG Speaker Wire, 50 ft
items.desc: 50 feet of red and black copper wire that connects the amplifier to the speakers.

items.name: USB Logic Analyzer, 8-Channel
items.desc: A USB tool that records up to eight digital signals at once, so he can see exactly what chips are saying to each other when debugging a circuit.

items.name: Autoranging Digital Multimeter
items.desc: A pocket-size meter that picks its own range to measure voltage, current and resistance. An everyday tool for checking circuits.

items.name: Mac mini (M6, 16GB, 256GB)
items.note: Apple Education Store price; $899 at the regular Apple Store.
items.desc: Apple Mac mini with the M6 chip, 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, 16GB memory and 256GB storage.

items.name: Raspberry Pi 5 Starter Kit (4GB)
items.desc: A Raspberry Pi 5 (4GB) with a 27W power supply, a 32GB SD card with the operating system already installed, and an actively cooled aluminum case. A small Linux computer for projects and learning.

items.name: DJI Mic Mobile Receiver (USB-C), works with Mic 2
items.note: DJI's page lists it as compatible with DJI Mic 2 transmitters. In stock at Amazon on Nov 26 (sold by a third-party seller); sold out at the DJI Store.
items.desc: A small USB-C receiver that plugs into his iPhone and picks up his DJI Mic 2 wireless microphone, so he can record clear audio for videos.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 ×2
items.desc: A 12-megapixel camera with autofocus that plugs into a Raspberry Pi. One will watch his 3D printer for layer-by-layer timelapses and the other will look down at papers to scan them.

items.name: Camera Cable, 22-pin to 15-pin ×2
items.desc: A thin flat cable that connects the camera to the small camera port on a Raspberry Pi 5 or Pi Zero.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Starter Kit
items.note: Kit with a case; the bare board is sold out at Adafruit, PiShop and Vilros.
items.desc: A tiny, low-power computer with Wi-Fi, bundled with a case, that will run the 3D printer timelapse camera.

items.name: Micro Servo, metal gear ×4
items.desc: Small motors that turn to a precise angle, with metal gears for strength. Four of them run from his servo driver board to move robot joints.
items.note: $9.95 each, four wanted. Adafruit's cheaper plastic-gear servo was sold out.

items.name: Heart-Rate & Pulse Oximeter Sensor
items.desc: A plug-in sensor that shines light through a fingertip to measure heart rate and blood oxygen. It does the math on the board and connects with one cable, no soldering.

items.name: APDS9960 Gesture & Color Sensor
items.desc: Detects hand swipes in the air, how close something is, and the color and brightness of light. Plugs in with one cable, no soldering.

items.name: BME688 Environment Sensor
items.desc: Measures temperature, humidity, air pressure and air quality (gases) in one tiny board. Plugs in with one cable, no soldering.

items.name: Mini GPS Module (PA1010D)
items.desc: A small GPS receiver that reports where it is, how fast it's moving and the time. Plugs in with one cable, no soldering.

items.name: Rotary Encoder with Lights
items.desc: A click-and-turn knob with a colored light inside, useful as a dial or menu control. Plugs in with one cable, no soldering.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2, 10.1 inch
items.desc: The official 10.1-inch touchscreen for a Raspberry Pi, for a desk or wall dashboard. It's 9.8 by 6.5 inches, a little narrower than an iPad.

items.name: 2.13" E-Ink Display (tri-color)
items.desc: A paper-like black, white and red screen that keeps its image with no power, and plugs onto his Feather board. Good for a small always-on display.
items.note: The all-in-one Adafruit MagTag e-ink display was sold out at Adafruit and Amazon on Nov 26.

items.name: 1.12" OLED Display
items.desc: A small, sharp black-and-white screen that connects with one cable, no soldering. For showing readings and menus.

items.name: ESP32-S3 TFT Feather (color screen)
items.desc: A programmable board with a small color screen already built in, plus Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Plugs into his other sensors with one cable.
items.note: Adafruit has no color screen that plugs in over a single cable, so this board with the screen built in is the closest match.

items.name: Mini Gamepad (plug-in)
items.desc: A tiny controller with a direction pad and buttons that connects with one cable, no soldering. For games and menus on his projects.

items.name: Arcade Button with LED ×4
items.desc: Big, clicky arcade-style buttons with a light inside, for control panels and game builds.

items.name: Pinecil V2 Soldering Iron
items.desc: A small, fast-heating soldering iron with a digital display, powered from a USB-C charger. For joining wires and parts onto circuit boards.

items.name: Lead-Free Solder Wire, thin (50 g)
items.desc: A spool of thin lead-free solder, the metal that melts to join parts. Fine enough for small circuit boards.

items.name: No-Clean Flux Pen
items.desc: A pen that paints on flux, which helps solder flow so joints come out clean and shiny.

items.name: Brass Soldering Tip Cleaner
items.desc: A holder of brass shavings for wiping the soldering iron tip clean without cooling it.

items.name: Helping Hands with Magnifier
items.desc: Adjustable clips and a magnifying glass that hold a circuit board steady while he solders.

items.name: Heat-Proof Silicone Work Mat
items.desc: A heat-resistant mat that protects the desk and keeps small parts from rolling away while soldering.

items.name: MyoWare 2.0 Link Shield
items.desc: A small board that snaps onto the muscle sensor and brings its signal out through a standard headphone-style jack.
items.note: Needs the cable and breakout below to reach his board.

items.name: 3.5 mm Audio Cable, 1 m
items.desc: A plain headphone-style cable that carries the muscle sensor's signal from the Link Shield to the breakout board.

items.name: Headphone Jack Breakout Board
items.desc: A small board that turns the headphone jack into pins his board can connect to, so the cable can plug in. Needs a few header pins soldered on.
